description: ol-undefined-var (issue #825, block lifetime): a name born INSIDE a block goes out of scope at the end of that block, so no code outside it can name that binding (spec/execution-model.md:603-615). `:i` is created in the `repeat` body — fresh on every turn — and the read after the `]` resolves against nothing, at the read's own span. It is `ol-undefined-var`, not `ol-var-not-visible`: the read is at the top level, where there is no procedure boundary to be the cause. The non-regression this must not break is the accumulator idiom, where `:total` is born OUTSIDE the block and all four turns update one binding — pinned by tests/conformance/core-language/scoping/a-block-updates-what-it-can-see.
